svg.text: Rotary Phone → Pico (RP2040) — Rev F (AC-couples receiver via C5, D1 restricted to 1N4148, adds C6 hook filter, 2026-07-26)
Dial fully isolated from phone network. WHITE = shunt/off-normal (N1), BLUE = pulse (N2), GREEN/WHITE = switchhook lever (N3), RED/BLACK = carbon mic (N4), WHITE/GREEN = receiver (N5).
Every dashed box below is a component that physically lives inside the phone (handset or dial); everything outside the dashed boxes is the discrete circuit you are building on/around the Pico.
Phase 0 DMM result: mic resistance ~0.5–2kΩ baseline, drifting with ambient sound, spiking 5kΩ+ on shock — confirms carbon mic. Receiver (earpiece) ~50–300Ω electromagnetic coil.
Pin.PULL_UP enabled in software (GP3, GP4 only)
under the handset cradle — GREEN/WHITE pair (N3)
audio modulates duty; coil filters carrier.
C5 blocks the ~11mA DC bias a bare 50%-duty
drive would push through the coil — protects the

S3 is a true dry contact (DMM confirmed: ≈0Ω pressed, open released), same as BLUE. Internal Pin.PULL_UP on GP4 is sufficient; C6 100nF to GND adds EMI immunity for the long handset cord (RC ≈ 5–8ms).
Lever PRESSED (handset resting) = on-hook = GP4 LOW (closed to GND) = MUTE (main.py sends a 0% volume HID report, remembering the last dialed target).
Lever RELEASED (handset lifted) = off-hook = GP4 HIGH (pulled to 3V3) = firmware restores the last dialed volume target automatically.
Debounce: 30ms (heavier lever spring than the dial contacts, which use 15ms). Polarity within the GREEN/WHITE pair does not matter.
Mic + receiver front end — Phase 0 status & next steps
Phase 0 COMPLETE: DMM confirms carbon mic (dynamic 0.5–2kΩ, spikes 5kΩ+) across RED/BLACK; receiver expected 50–300Ω across WHITE/GREEN — verify with DMM before wiring.
No amplifier IC anywhere: the carbon mic self-amplifies via its DC bias current (R4), and the high-impedance receiver coil is switched directly by one NPN transistor.
Any film/polyester/polypropylene caps on hand are fine for C3 (coupling) and C4 (filter); use electrolytic for the bulk C1 (100μF) bias decoupling — film at that value is unnecessarily large.
Next: Phase 1/2 wiring per this diagram, then Phase 3 firmware stages (PWM tone test → mic RMS meter → local sidetone loopback → USB streaming, last).

Component hunt list: R4 220–330Ω, R5 4.7k, R6/R7 2×100k, R8 1k (optional 47–100Ω series w/ coil); C1 100μF, C2 100nF, C3 1–10μF, C4 10nF, C5 100μF electrolytic, C6 100nF; one general NPN; one 1N4148 (NOT 1N400x — t_rr too slow for 125kHz).
